title: Predictive tenant steering: soft-commit reservations, staged demotions, and hosted-fallback contracts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a predictive tenant steering system that reserves soft-capacity lanes on dedicated clusters based on short-horizon load forecasts, and executes staged model-variant demotions with a contractual hosted fallback path when tight capacity or latency SLOs are predicted to be violated. Goal: reduce abrupt tenant preemption, minimize costly hosted spill decisions made at request time, and provide predictable fallbacks with measurable SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive allocator runs every 30s and produces per-tenant soft-commit tokens with TTL and confidence score
Routing layer consumes soft-commit tokens and prefers soft-reserved lanes for requests while honoring latency SLOs
Staged demotion pipeline can demote model variants in three discrete steps (full-precision -> quantized -> smaller-arch) with rollback hooks
Hosted fallback contract defined: latency threshold, cost cap, and timeout behavior tested end-to-end in staging
Automated canary: 5 tenants in staging routed through predictive steering for 48h with SLI telemetry showing no >5% error increase
Runbook created for emergency forced-evacuation and reverse rollouts

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive reservation reduces last-second failovers but raises dedicated idle cost; we favor short TTL (30-90s) and confidence-driven issuance to balance.
Testing plan: fault-inject predictor failure, token-store partition, and hosted region outage to validate graceful degradation paths.
Security: tokens contain no secrets; they are capability descriptors with HMAC signed metadata for tamper protection (spec to follow).

Runbook highlights: (1) If demotion causes QoE regression >5% open rollback, (2) If fallback-cost burn > threshold trigger tenant throttle policy, (3) For sustained cloud-wide overload, enable global demotion lockstep and halt new token issues.
